questions.q: Which London club was Phileas Fogg a member of?
choices: The Reform Club
The Royal Institution
The Artisan's Association
The London Institution
questions.evidence: Phileas Fogg was a member of the Reform, and that was all.

questions.q: What did the people who knew Phileas Fogg NOT know about his money?
choices: How he had made his fortune in the first place
Which London bank he kept his account with
Whether he gave any of it away to good causes
Whether he had enough to belong to a club

questions.q: Fogg "seemed all the more mysterious for his taciturn manner." What does taciturn mean here?
choices: Rude and quick to argue
Saying very little
Nervous and easily upset
Cheerful and joking
questions.evidence: He talked very little, and seemed all the more mysterious for his taciturn manner.

questions.q: What did Fogg do with the money he won playing whist?
choices: He spent it on fine wine at the club
He saved it in the safe in his bedroom
He kept it as a fund for his charities
He used it to pay his servant's wages
questions.evidence: his winnings never went into his purse, being reserved as a fund for his charities

questions.q: Why did Fogg play whist, according to the chapter?
choices: To win money from the other club members
For the sake of playing, as a quiet struggle with a difficulty
To make friends among the members of the Reform
Because his doctor told him to rest his mind each night
questions.evidence: Mr. Fogg played, not to win, but for the sake of playing.

questions.q: Where did Fogg eat his breakfast and dinner?

At a different restaurant in the City each day
At the club, at the same table at fixed hours
At the homes of his few close friends in London
questions.evidence: He breakfasted and dined at the club, at hours mathematically fixed

He brought shaving-water two degrees too cool
He forgot to wind the clock in the bedroom
He laid out the wrong suit for the season
questions.evidence: brought him shaving-water at eighty-four degrees Fahrenheit instead of eighty-six
